cells.tense: You are deciding the direction at the bench right now, and the deciding is calm.
cells.ask: Pick one standing practice, write the finish line on paper, and keep the paper where you work.
cells.core:
The direction is yours and it's steady. You sit down and choose what to sharpen, what to leave alone, what to stop touching — and it happens here, not in a story about later. That's the whole thing, and you have it. A small light, kept lit by showing up, turning intention into skill.

What holds it is endurance — carrying the slow stretch without forcing the pace. You can stay with this for the length it takes without going hard around it. So feed that next. Stay with the one thing worth staying with, and let the staying be the proof. The work doesn't need drama from you, just the next honest hour.

cells.tense: You will be bracing at a future that can't be written in yet.
cells.ask: This week, run the practice once at the pace it actually moves, and stop when the timer says stop, not when it feels finished.
cells.core:
You're living ahead of the bench. Somewhere out there is the version where the skill is finished, the outcome locked, the thing finally obeying — and you're already there, forcing the pace to meet it. So the practice turns into pushing, and pushing turns the craft into a fight you scheduled with yourself.

What's missing is seeing the whole shape without needing to close it. Look at what's actually in front of you, at the speed it actually moves, and let that be the measure. Direction doesn't need white knuckles. Hold the form and let it take the time it takes. Endurance that contains is still endurance.

cells.tense: You were standing at a door that had already closed behind you.
cells.ask: Do ten minutes of something you're already good at, no plan attached, and stop at ten even if it goes well.
cells.core:
The bench is there and you walk past it. Direction stopped landing, the practice thinned out, and now 'what's the point' answers before the question finishes. Nothing gets poured into this from effort alone — trying harder at the empty bench is the one move that won't work.

What fills it is doing the thing itself, expressed. Not practice for a result — practice because it's what you are. Do a small piece of it for its own sake, and let that count as the whole point. The light doesn't need to prove anything to be lit. Start at ten minutes and let the ten minutes be enough.
cells.sheetLine: The point isn't missing. The showing up is.

cells.tense: You are deciding while calling it the schedule deciding for you.
cells.ask: Before one session today, say out loud which part you're working on and why, then do it, and notice whether the reason was yours.
cells.core:
The practice happens, the thing gets refined, the direction gets set — and it all runs under the name of habit, or routine, or just how the days go. The pen is down and writing; the hand doesn't know it's holding it. You are picking, in there, and the picking is coming out as something that happens rather than something you did.

That's not a flaw in the work. It's a missing credit line. Somewhere in there is a reason you chose this and not that, and the reason has your name on it. Name one choice you made inside the routine and say it's yours. The light doesn't dim when you admit you lit it. It gets brighter, because now it's aimed.
cells.sheetLine: The picking is real. It can carry your name.
